# Types

## User fields

```sh
BITRIX_URL=https://portal.bitrix24.com/rest/1/WEBHOOK_TOKEN npx bitrix-types --out src/bitrix-user-fields.d.ts
```

User fields differ per portal, so out of the box `UF_*` fields are `unknown`. `bitrix-types` reads the user fields of deals, leads, contacts and companies and writes a declaration file for them:

```ts
// Generated by bitrix-types from https://portal.bitrix24.com. Run it again instead of editing this file.
import type { UserFieldFile } from '@2bad/bitrix'

declare module '@2bad/bitrix' {
  interface DealUserFields {
    /**
     * Payment terms
     * - 45: Prepaid
     * - 47: 50% and 50%
     */
    readonly UF_CRM_1565877516: '45' | '47' | null
    /** Contract */
    readonly UF_CRM_1640162732: UserFieldFile | null
  }
}
```

After that the fields are typed in `get`, `list`, `select` and the fields of `create` and `update`:

```ts
const deal = await bitrix.deals.get(77)
deal.UF_CRM_1565877516 // '45' | '47' | null

await bitrix.deals.update(77, {
  UF_CRM_1565877516: 47,
  UF_CRM_1640162732: { fileData: ['contract.pdf', base64] }
})
```

Single fields can be `null`. Multiple fields are arrays, or `false` when empty. Enumerations are item ids: strings in single fields, numbers in multiple ones. Field types added by apps are `unknown`. Run the command again after changing fields in the portal.

```sh
bitrix-types [--url <rest url>] [--out <file>] [--entities deal,lead,contact,company]
```

`--url` replaces `BITRIX_URL`, `BITRIX_TOKEN` sets an OAuth access token, no `--out` prints to stdout. The file only contains the portal address, never the token.

## Other methods

```ts
declare module '@2bad/bitrix' {
  interface Methods {
    'tasks.task.get': { params: { taskId: number; select?: string[] }; result: { task: Task } }
  }
}

const { task } = await bitrix.call('tasks.task.get', { taskId: 1 })
```

Methods in `Methods` get checked params and typed results in `call`, `list`, `paginate` and `batch`. Any other method still works with loose params and an `unknown` result.
